title: Cellulose extraction and quantification from eucalyptus leaves
author: Sophia Cain
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-2401/v1
materials: Move tubes to rack to cool.

steps.title: Grind leaf material
steps.instruction: Place a few eucalyptus leaves in a 20 mL polyethylene vial containing 4–5 metal beads, cap the vial, and grind the leaves using a cryogenic bead grinder.

steps.title: Prepare pierced microcentrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Using a pin or sharp tweezers, make two holes in the lid of a 2 mL round‑bottomed microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Weigh ground plant material
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 20 mg of the ground leaf material into the pierced 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Add digestion acids
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of 80 % (v/v) acetic acid (prepare from glacial acetic acid if needed) and 40 µL of 69 % (v/v) concentrated nitric acid to the tube; keep the lid open for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Seal and heat for digestion
steps.instruction: Cap the tube tightly, place it in a heating block that is initially at room temperature, set the block to 120 °C, and once the block reaches 120 °C, boil the samples for 30 minutes, tapping each tube every 5 minutes to prevent condensation buildup.

steps.title: Wash cellulose – ethanol
steps.instruction: Cover the lid holes with parafilm, add 1000 µL of ethanol, invert to mix, centrifuge 5 minutes at 7000 rpm, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash cellulose – water
steps.instruction: Repeat the washing procedure with 1000 µL of deionized water (cover holes, invert, centrifuge 5 min at 7000 rpm, discard supernatant).

steps.title: Dry washed cellulose
steps.instruction: Cover the rack of tubes with aluminium foil and let the samples dry in a fume hood overnight.

steps.title: Prepare 67 % sulfuric acid
steps.instruction: Slowly add 335 mL concentrated H₂SO₄ to 165 mL milli‑Q water (always acid to water), allow the solution to cool, and keep it ready for use.

steps.title: Add sulfuric acid to cellulose
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the freshly prepared 67 % sulfuric acid solution to each dried cellulose sample (add only for the number of samples processed that day).

steps.title: Shake cellulose suspension
steps.instruction: Shake the tubes at room temperature for 1 hour until no solid material is visible.

steps.title: Prepare glucose standards
steps.instruction: Prepare glucose standards at concentrations of 0, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 µg mL⁻¹ according to Kumar & Turner (2015).

steps.title: Transfer samples to 15 mL tubes
steps.instruction: In a new 15 mL screw‑capped tube, add 500 µL milli‑Q water, then add 20 µL of each cellulose‑derived sample; also aliquot 500 µL of each glucose standard into separate 2 mL screw‑capped tubes.

steps.title: Prepare anthrone reagent
steps.instruction: Over ice, prepare 100 mL of 0.3 % (w/v) anthrone solution in concentrated sulfuric acid (stable ~3 hours) and mix with a glass stirring rod.

steps.title: Add anthrone to samples and standards
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the anthrone solution to each test sample and standard by slowly dispensing down the side of the tube, cap tightly, and mix by inversion (tubes become very hot; wear appropriate PPE).

steps.title: Heat anthrone reaction
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a boiling water bath for exactly 5 minutes, then immediately cool them on ice (do not exceed 5 minutes to avoid colour loss).

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of each cooled reaction mixture to a microplate well and record absorbance at 620 nm (OD₆₂₀).

steps.title: Generate regression and calculate glucose
steps.instruction: Generate a regression curve from the glucose standard absorbance values and determine the glucose concentration of each sample.

steps.title: Calculate cellulose content
steps.instruction: Calculate cellulose percentage using Equation 1: Cellulose (% of ground plant material) = glucose (µg mL⁻¹) / (weight of sample (µg) × 100 × 50).
